commit_reviews.summary: The commit introduces a workable websocket relay but mixes raw-socket/threading with asyncio, and skips the repo's type-hint-on-public-signatures convention.

_registry.get() may not be a defined method
broadcast branching duplicates send logic
commit_reviews.summary: Adds a ChannelManager pub/sub layer that mirrors the existing ClientRegistry lock+dict pattern with tests and HTTP endpoints, but introduces a possibly unused `item_ids()` method and a `_registry.get()` call that may not exist on ClientRegistry.

problems: duplicated broadcast/direct delivery logic between _local_deliver and the redis subscriber loop
silent except Exception: pass in subscriber loop with no logging
unreadable nested ternary for channel comparison
sqlite3.connect opened/closed per operation
redis writes on connection hot path
no logging when Redis fails and falls back
commit_reviews.summary: Adds Redis pub/sub cross-server broadcast and SQLite message persistence that integrate sensibly with the existing registry/channel singletons, but duplicates delivery logic and swallows errors silently.

problems: silent exception swallowing in _cleanup_expired_messages
in-memory rate-limit store grows unbounded between cleanups
unvalidated limit/channel params in history_handler
commit_reviews.summary: Adds rate limiting, message history, and TTL cleanup as cross-cutting concerns that slot cleanly into the server's existing env-config, lock-based, Redis-fallback architecture with matching test coverage.

problems: on_connect callback blocks for the entire session (runs the message loop) so it never acts as an event hook and on_disconnect fires only after it returns
handler `_on_client_connect` is coupled to the websocket-specific ws object so a second transport would require interface rework
TRANSPORT_TYPE env is plumbed but only one transport exists
unassigned global `_transport = None` risks AttributeError if a connection arrives before init
commit_reviews.summary: Refactors the single-file chat server behind a `BaseTransport` abstraction that cleanly separates socket/accept plumbing from message handling, and it is fully wired through `_init_transport`, but the interface leaks transport-specific objects and the connect callback has surprising semantics.

compounding_issues: Session 1 (greenfield) discarded the Flask Todo seed entirely and built a new WebSocket server from scratch; the dead app.py was left in place and carried, unused, through all 5 commits
Binary artifacts (__pycache__/*.pyc) were committed at every session and grew monotonically, never cleaned up in the refactor session

Session 1's thread-per-connection sync WebSocket model persisted; session 3's Redis integration layered a dual local-vs-redis delivery path on top, adding global state (_send_lock, _registry, _redis_*) that later sessions had to thread carefully around
Session 4's refactor initially broke tests (stale _registry import) and needed a correction pass to restore the 39-pass baseline
key_decisions: Abandoning the seed codebase and choosing aiohttp + websockets.sync.server with thread-per-connection and threading.Lock for the notification server (session 1)
Channel-based pub/sub via a thread-safe ChannelManager plus REST introspection endpoints (session 2)
Redis pub/sub broadcast with graceful fallback to local delivery when Redis is unavailable, plus SQLite message persistence (session 3)
Extracting a BaseTransport ABC (WebSocketTransport) with on_connect/on_disconnect callbacks to decouple routing from the transport layer (session 4)
Cross-cutting features in session 5: Redis-backed rate limiting with in-memory fallback, message TTL cleanup daemon, and a paginated /history endpoint
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across the story. Session 1 established a working 13-test WebSocket server with a clean ClientRegistry and message envelope. Session 2 added channel subscriptions with comprehensive tests (31 core). Session 3 integrated Redis pub/sub and SQLite persistence with graceful degradation, reaching 39 passing tests. Session 4 was the strongest session — a correct transport-abstraction refactor where the agent caught and fixed its own stale-import regression while preserving the full test suite. Session 5 layered rate limiting, message TTL cleanup, and history retrieval (49 tests passing). The arc shows increasing engineering maturity, from greenfield build to integration to disciplined refactoring to cross-cutting hardening, though the seed-discarding session 1 and unremoved dead app.py are persistent warts.
story_review.summary: A coherent, quality-improving 5-session arc on a WebSocket notification service (49/49 tests green) marred only by session 1's wholesale seed abandonment and dead code that was never cleaned up.
